root_idea.summary: The root centers on lightness and promptness in action together with coming together or coordinated assistance.
root_idea.development: The semantic orientation develops from swift, well-coordinated movement to prompt service and the helpers who provide it; related formations also preserve notions of causative acceleration, being served, and swift cutting.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form حَافِدٌ; the Quranic occurrence itself is the plural حَفَدَةً.

quranic_forms.public_pos_label: Active participle · plural حفدة in Quran

senses.definition: Helpers, assistants, or attendants who move promptly to serve and work in obedience.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction of 16:72, حَفَدَة is the plural of حَافِد and may denote relatives or outsiders characterized by voluntary, active service.
An alternative traditional interpretation of حَفَدَة in 16:72; the term may refer especially to sons’ children, without making that specification obligatory in every usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move quickly or maintain a quick, continuous pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical descriptions illustrate sustained rapid movement; they do not restrict the verb to one particular animal or object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be active, agile, or prompt in an affair, work, or service.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The emphasis is on energetic and prompt performance, including readiness to obey or serve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To serve and work for another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional verbal use describing service performed for a person; it is distinct from merely moving quickly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or incite another, especially an animal, to move quickly with a continuous pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative Form IV use of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pace less quick than one termed خَبَبٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal designation for a degree or kind of pace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that moves quickly with a continuous pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent or descriptive noun formed from the speed branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In extended kinship usage, children or daughters; also children and grandchildren who serve a parent, in-laws, or a wife’s sons by an earlier husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are alternative Classical Arabic extensions of the helper and kinship vocabulary, not a single obligatory referent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person’s origin, lineage, or ancestral base.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote origin in a general sense, as well as a person’s lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The base or lower part of a camel’s hump, or the hump itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete anatomical use distinct from the meaning ‘origin’ or ‘lineage’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is served, attended, honored, and obeyed by others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description emphasizes companions or associates hastening to serve and honor him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword that is quick in cutting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or descriptive use applied to the speed and effectiveness of a sword’s cut.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Prompt activity in work, affairs, and service.
Descriptive noun for a swiftly moving camel.
Helper, grandchild, and extended kinship branches.
A person attended and obeyed by others.

cautions: حَفَدَةٌ in 16:72 has materially different traditional interpretations: helpers or attendants on one reading, and grandchildren or descendants on another. The supplied contextual gloss reflects the latter interpretation but does not by itself settle the lexical question.
The Quranic form is the plural حَفَدَةً; حَافِدٌ is used here as the normalized singular dictionary citation form.
